source_locators: Demand-management section: peak summer consumption fell from about 1,200 MLD in 2015 to about 500 MLD in 2018 against a 450 MLD target.
Restriction chronology: Level 6B applied from 1 February through 30 September 2018 with a 50 litre-per-person daily limit and four million represented residents.
Drought-tariff annex: approximately ZAR 1.7 billion anticipated water-service revenue under-recovery in 2017/18.
Restriction transition summary: Level 5 began 1 October 2018 and Level 3 began 1 December 2018, confirming the end boundary of Level 6B.

transformations.formula: Subtract the utility-reported 2018 actual demand of about 500 MLD from the reported 2015 summer peak of about 1,200 MLD, retaining the 450 MLD restricted target and 50 MLD target exceedance.
Use the City-reported ZAR 1.7 billion anticipated water-service revenue under-recovery; do not substitute total provincial drought losses.
Use the three-year February 2015 to February 2018 peak-demand comparison period.
Normalize the City-reported four-million-person service population; do not extrapolate one utility to national or global coverage.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The Outlook reports approximate peak-demand values and a municipal target, so the derived reduction and exceedance inherit rounding. The ZAR 1.7 billion value is anticipated water-service revenue under-recovery, not total drought damage. Four million is the City’s represented population calculation for the 50-litre limit, not a connection count. Level 6B was a formal restriction and conservation limit; Day Zero shutoff was a contingency that did not occur. Coverage is one metropolitan service area in one country.
receipts.freshness: Cape Town 2018 drought episode; official reports reviewed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: The City utility report quantifies summer peak demand, actual demand, its restricted target, service-revenue burden, a multi-year management period and represented population within a named service area.
higher_priority_failures: The observation is a dated metropolitan accumulated-impact episode, not a current global utility-demand aggregation.
The three annual peak points do not satisfy the 20-annual-observation historical-distribution gate.
